content.text: {"relation":"REFINED","consensus_summary":"Door/gate primarily symbolizes access to God and salvation, with Christ himself as the exclusive door (John 10:9) through whom believers enter eternal life; secondary uses include the narrow gate of discipleship, open doors of ministry opportunity, the door of the heart, city gates as civic power/judgment, and eschatological shut doors.","book_summary":"Jesus as the destination of the Way and the threshold into the covenant house, whose posts are marked by blood (Passover) and the word of God (Deut 6:9); additionally, heaven's gates are identified with the constellations through which the New Moon appears monthly, tied to the twelve gates of Rev 21:12-13.","consensus_core_identification":"Christ as the exclusive door/entrance to salvation and fellowship with God; the gate as the point of access and boundary between admitted and excluded.","book_core_identification":"Jesus as the door/threshold into the covenant house (salvation/God's household), with the door marked typologically by blood and the word, and extended cosmically to heaven's gates as lunar/constellational stations.","core_relation":"EQUIVALENT","extension_relation":"BOOK_SUPERSET","boundary_disagreement":"The book adds cases the consensus does not cover: (1) it foregrounds the Passover blood-marked doorposts and Deut 6:9 word-marked posts as constitutive of the symbol (a typological reading only a minority alternative in Response A), and (2) it introduces an astronomical extension, reading 'heaven's gates' (Gen 28:17; Rev 21:12-13) as the constellations through which the New Moon appears each month — a calendrical/cosmological referent absent from all consensus responses and alternatives.","material_contradiction":"None at the core. The book affirms rather than replaces the consensus identification of Jesus as the door of salvation; the constellation claim is additive, not a denial of the Christological center.","rationale":"Reduced to minimum cores, both readings identify Jesus as the door/entrance into salvation and the covenant household — an equivalent center, explicitly grounded in the same John 10:9 text. However, the book materially changes the symbol's extension by binding the door to the marked doorposts (blood and word) as part of its definition, and by admitting a wholly new class of referents: heaven's gates as constellations governing the monthly New Moon appearance, apparently linked to the twelve directional gates of the New Jerusalem. No consensus response or alternative includes any astronomical-calendrical meaning. Because the central referent survives intact while the covered cases are broadened in a specific, non-trivial way, REFINED (not MATCH, since the additions are material; not NOVEL, since the core is squarely within consensus) is correct.","citation_support":"PARTIAL","strongest_objection":"One could argue MATCH, since the book's core (Jesus as the door into salvation) is exactly the consensus primary meaning and the astronomical remark could be dismissed as decorative detail; alternatively, one could argue the constellation claim is significant enough to warrant NOVEL for that component. PARTIAL/REFINED balances these: the printed citations (John 10:9, Ex 12:7, Deut 6:9, Gen 28:17, Rev 21:12-13) support the Christological-typological core well, but nothing in them states or implies that heaven's gates mark constellations or the New Moon's monthly appearance — that reading is imported, not exhibited by the texts.","confidence":"high"}
